problems.source_says: The paper explicitly reports stratified random assignment to four conditions, but does not identify the allocation unit or explain when and how dyads were formed. Individual-level rather than dyad-level allocation cannot be explicitly confirmed; the allocation unit should remain unspecified.
problems.quote: Importantly, conditions were assigned using a stratified randomization procedure accounting for prior AI exposure, job function, and digital fluency.
problems.locator: PDF p. 5 (index 4), Methodology, Procedures, recruitment/randomization paragraph and subsequent task-procedure paragraph; full document including Appendix A checked.

problems.form_value: The no-AI arms received no corresponding training.
problems.source_says: The paper specifies a 45-minute prompt-engineering and GPT-4 training module for those assigned to AI. It does not describe what the no-AI groups did during this interval or explicitly state that they received no corresponding training; absence of comparable control training is unconfirmed.
problems.quote: Those assigned to the AI condition then undertook a 45-minute training module on prompt engineering and hands-on interaction with GPT-4.
problems.locator: PDF p. 5 (index 4), Methodology, Procedures, paragraph beginning "The experiment was conducted in a controlled virtual environment"; full document including Appendix A checked.

confirmed.statement: S1 explicitly reports stratified randomization accounting for prior AI exposure, job function, and digital fluency.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 5, Methodology, Procedures, recruitment/randomization paragraph; p. 1, Abstract.

confirmed.statement: S1 manipulates GenAI availability (present versus absent) crossed with collaboration structure (individual versus team).
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 5, Methodology, Procedures, first paragraph.

confirmed.statement: The four arms and their reported Table 2 Ns match the form: Individual No AI 92, Team No AI 95, Individual AI 90, and Team AI 94.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 6, Table 2, Group and N columns; p. 5, Procedures, solo/dyad task description.

confirmed.statement: GPT-4 is the named tool, and the document identifies GPT-4 as a large language model.

confirmed.statement: AI participants received a 45-minute prompt-engineering and hands-on GPT-4 training module before the 90-minute problem-solving phase.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 5, Procedures, paragraph beginning "The experiment was conducted in a controlled virtual environment".

confirmed.statement: Participants used their own prompts for drafting and exploring innovation proposals; AI assistance concerned their own work, not merely the origin of outputs shown to evaluators.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 5, Procedures and Measures; p. 7, Illustrative cases of assimilation vs. accommodation, participant accounts and prompt histories.

confirmed.statement: The no-AI comparison is explicitly reported for both individual and team conditions.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 5, Procedures, GenAI availability present versus absent; p. 6, Table 2 and Effects of GenAI and collaboration structure.

confirmed.statement: S1 compares separate conditions on a single innovation task; the form correctly treats it as between participants, so within-person condition-order randomization is not applicable.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 5-6, Procedures and Table 2; p. 9, Limitations and future research, first paragraph.

confirmed.statement: Assimilation and accommodation were classified from post-task surveys and qualitative evidence, rather than assigned as experimental arms.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 5, Measures, first two paragraphs; p. 10, Appendix A, post-task cognitive-strategy items.

summary: The paper explicitly supports random assignment to generative-AI assistance for participants' own innovation work, so criterion 1 holds. The form nevertheless asserts an individual allocation unit and no corresponding control-group training without explicit documentation of either detail.
